xrunner is now **xcrunner**: the command, the PyPI package, the settings and the folders. This release also adds experimental macOS support and three features that help on every platform.

    pip install xcrunner

## The rename

This is a clean break. Nothing reads the old names.

- The command is `xcrunner`. The PyPI package is `xcrunner`; `xc-xrunner` gets no more releases. Uninstall it first: `pip uninstall xc-xrunner`.
- Every `XRUNNER_*` setting is now `XCRUNNER_*`, for example `XCRUNNER_ENV_DIR`.
- A project's env folder is now `.xcrunner-env`. An existing `.xrunner-env` is not used; rename it, or let xcrunner start a new one.
- The engine value in coala and coala-runtime is `xcrunner`, and coala-runtime's extra is `[xcrunner]`.
- The repository is `xcodon-ai/xcrunner`. The Python module is still `xcodon_runtime`, and the `XCODON_*` settings keep their names.

## macOS (experimental)

xcrunner now runs on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or newer. It runs the Linux xcrunner inside one Lima VM.

    brew install lima
    pip install xcrunner
    xcrunner machine start
    xcrunner run --rm alpine echo hi

- The first `xcrunner machine start` creates an Ubuntu 24.04 VM with Rosetta. Your home folder, `/private/var/folders` and `/private/tmp` are shared into it at the same paths.
- `conda`, `shim`, `sandbox` and `machine` run on the Mac. Every other command runs in the VM, with the same exit code and output.
- `xcrunner machine start|stop|status|shell|rm` manage the VM. The `XCRUNNER_MACHINE_*` settings set its size and extra shared folders.
- This release was tested on Linux against a fake Lima only. It has not run on a real Mac yet. `scripts/mac_smoke.sh` runs the end-to-end checks on a Mac; please report what fails.

## All platforms

- **`XCRUNNER_ENV_LAYER_DIR`** keeps env folder layers on another disk, while the environment record stays in the project. On a cluster, point it at node-local disk.
- **x86_64 images on ARM hosts.** With a Rosetta or qemu-x86_64 handler registered, an image list without an ARM image falls back to x86_64.
- **Pull-time architecture check.** An image the host cannot run now fails at pull time with a clear message, instead of failing later with "exec format error". An explicit `--platform` skips the check.
- **Conda shim on macOS ARM.** The shim pins micromamba 2.9.0 for `osx-arm64` as well as `linux-64`. A failed install on a Mac suggests `--platform osx-64`.
